source_correspondence: R0 specifies a finite tangential Sobolev order rather than H1 for the comparison distribution, with all tangential source orders, actual smooth value data and a regular incoming germ in one fixed source region.

R1 proves actual traces at every real index and gives an explicit two-jet half-space extension. The Fourier identity puts the distribution in restriction H(2,s-2), so the elliptic left identity has its required normal domain. Actual trace commutations include derivatives of every parameter cutoff.

R2 retains the complete matrix root, transported test and source formula. Its actual negative-order trace determines the exact weak Duhamel evolution. Full Cauchy wavefront and transverse trace arguments therefore control both entire incoming supports from the regular cap.

R3 verifies the actual H2 regularized equation at any finite starting index. Every full smoothing source coefficient acts on the original finite-order input and its normal derivative. The full Green identity, matrix damping, smooth value-trace errors and favorable exact normal square yield the half-gain without assuming an energy realization of the original comparison.

R4 uses the legitimate mixed elliptic domain and the exact one-order left-error gain; one application yields a full tangential derivative. Transverse reflection retains full matrix evolution. The explicit all-real finite-normal cone comparison repairs the positive-index shortcut in the earlier interior argument.

R5 iterates on the same open accessible region, using its geometric subpath property before any order is chosen. Local gains at every point and a finite parametrix cover imply each region-wide half-step. Actual normal traces become smooth on one fixed boundary patch.

R6 subtracts only the actual localized value-trace Dirichlet parametrix. ADT finite-loss action proves its finite starting order, actual traces and smooth residual. The full positive-root wavefront relation avoids the negative-normal cap. Outer cutoff commutators are retained outside the fixed assertion plateau. No two-tempered-mode representation is used.

R7 identifies the actual full Robin row from the now regular Dirichlet difference. Its two-sided boundary inverse is applied as a distributional identity before claiming finite output norms. Uniform boundary-collar regularity and complete compressed order comparison return to the actual H1 input.

R8 retains the original natural-dual source, boundary-preserving representative, full normal gauge and elliptic correction. Complex conjugation reverses every lower derivative sign and replaces M by minus its conjugate. Together with the earlier Dirichlet theorem this gives both-domain strict diffractive singular segments.

Three complete exercises verify both extension jets and their delta consequences, seven finite half-steps on one region, and both ordered products of a full nilpotent matrix Robin inverse. Thirty-five exact checks include all Hamilton equations, the characteristic constraint and the signed physical-time projection.

All thirteen overlapping desktop captures, the full original figure and two mobile samples were inspected. All 284 formulas, 33 displays and mobile display/figure extents pass. The figure retains the exact cap (25/96,1/16), Hamilton direction and omitted spatial coordinate.
